items.title: You’re Not Scaling Content. You’re Scaling Disappointment
items.summary: Pedro Dias traces the recurring cycle of mass-produced SEO content and explains why the 'publish more pages' playbook always ends in disappointment. Scaling quantity often leads to low-quality output that fails to rank or engage, undermining long-term content marketing success. Marketers should prioritize strategic, high-value content creation instead.

items.title: 3 CMS Platforms Control 73% Of The Market & Shape Technical SEO Defaults
items.summary: Three CMS platforms dominate 73% of the web market, dictating technical SEO defaults that influence optimization strategies worldwide. SEO professionals must understand these platforms' built-in settings to maximize impact. This shift highlights where technical tweaks yield the most value in modern SEO.

items.title: How AI Agents Decide Which Brands To Recommend: Trust Is The New Ranking Factor
items.summary: AI agents prioritize trust signals like E-E-A-T when recommending brands in search responses, evolving beyond traditional rankings. Building genuine authority through external validations is key for AI visibility. This marks a shift in SEO and content strategies toward credibility in AI-driven environments.

items.title: AI Search Generates 45 Billion Monthly Sessions Worldwide
items.summary: A Graphite.io study shows AI tools hitting 45 billion monthly sessions, 56% of global search volume, mostly via mobile apps. ChatGPT leads, with Gemini surging 237% YoY, as 37% of users start queries in AI chatbots. SEOs must expand tracking to AI visibility amid growing total search pie.

items.title: Niche Gaming Site Excels in Google Discover After Core Update
items.summary: Lily Ray highlights a niche gaming site's strong Google Discover performance with 15+ years of original human content, improving post-Discover core update. This case demonstrates enduring value of quality, specialized content in recommendation feeds. Discover remains vital for SEO and content discovery.

items.title: Open-Source /ai-seo Skill Optimizes Content for AI Engine Citations
items.summary: Corey Haines launches /ai-seo for Claude Code, auditing pages for LLM signals like structured data to boost citations in ChatGPT, Perplexity, and AI Overviews. It provides prioritized fixes, distinct from traditional SEO. Free as part of 32 marketing skills for AI agents.

items.title: Grammarly's AI 'Expert Review' Feature Accused of Impersonating Tech Journalists
items.summary: Tech journalist Ray Wong exposed Grammarly's AI feature for using his name, photo, and Gizmodo affiliation without permission to simulate his editing suggestions by scraping his past articles. He described it as identity theft, criticizing the company's disclaimer as insufficient. The viral post sparked calls for lawsuits and discussions on AI ethics in writing and editing tools.

items.title: Scarlett Press Secures Six-Figure Pre-Empt Deal for Georgia Bowers' Two Books
items.summary: Scarlett Press, an imprint of Simon & Schuster UK, acquired two books from author Georgia Bowers in a six-figure pre-empt deal at the London Book Fair. The announcement highlights major contracting activity in publishing. Shared by The Bookseller with link to full details.

items.title: BookTok Shifts Toward Older Backlist Books and Long Novels
items.summary: Exposed Books highlights a trend on BookTok where the canon is favoring older backlist titles and classics like Lonesome Dove, driven by algorithms, social proof, and desire for slow-burn immersion. Publishers are capitalizing on resurgent titles emphasizing emotional depth. This reflects a push for substantial reading experiences amid fast-scroll culture.

items.title: New AI licensing scheme helps smaller publishers strike deals with platforms
items.summary: Publishers’ Licensing Services (PLS) launched an opt-in collective licensing scheme for UK publishers to monetize content for AI training via an online store. Open to books, magazines, and news, it enables smaller publishers to access AI markets fairly. The initiative addresses growing demands from AI companies for licensed content.

items.title: Authors Protest AI at London Book Fair with ‘Empty’ Book
items.summary: Over 10,000 British writers, including Kazuo Ishiguro, published an empty book 'Don’t Steal This Book' to protest AI firms using their works without permission for training. They urge rejection of UK opt-out laws allowing mass copying, arguing it harms creators' earnings. The action demands fair pay from the AI industry built on 'stolen' content.

items.title: Oscars 2026: Has Hollywood’s “wokeism” run its course?
items.summary: Audience backlash against "wokeism" in Hollywood entertainment peaked at the 2026 Oscars and related award shows, with viewers expressing exhaustion and irritation over relentless moral grandstanding and virtue signaling from celebrities on social and political issues. This sentiment intensified following incidents like Billie Eilish's Grammy speech criticizing ICE, which drew accusations of hypocrisy due to her lifestyle, leading to widespread criticism of performative activism. Viewership declines for award ceremonies, including a 7% drop in Oscars ratings from 2025, underscore growing audience fatigue with such messaging.

items.title: Is #MeToo dead? Oscars 'asphyxiated' viewers with wokeness before spiral into 'implosion' of irrelevance, expert says
items.summary: Reputation management expert Eric Schiffer stated that the Academy has asphyxiated half its audience with preachy woke celebrities and gloating social justice gestures, contributing to a spiral into irrelevance amid a hostile political climate. He highlighted that overpoliticization and out-of-touch celebrity elitism alienate average Americans, with Hollywood treating the Oscars stage like a platform for self-absorbed political marauding that Middle America mocks. Schiffer anticipates another political showing this year, predicting at least one winner will turn the stage into a drive-by on half the country, further impacting viewership.

items.title: Rachel Zegler Says ‘Snow White’ Casting Backlash Was ‘Really Confusing’ and ‘I Refuse to Assimilate for Anybody Else’s Comfort’
items.summary: Rachel Zegler addressed the backlash to her casting in Disney's Snow White remake, describing it as confusing given criticisms related to her Colombian heritage after being told she wasn't enough for West Side Story. She emphasized her pride in her background and refusal to assimilate for others' comfort amid threats to her safety. The remarks follow reports of the film's financial loss linked to audience rejection.

items.title: Oscars slammed online for endless ‘virtue signaling’ from ‘woke’ Hollywood filmmakers
items.summary: Online users criticized the Oscars for featuring preachy speeches where filmmakers urged a moral choice against government actions and media oligarchs. The clip highlights virtue signaling that drew backlash against woke Hollywood elements. Audience reactions focused on the event's shift from entertainment to political commentary.

items.title: The culture war was everywhere just over a year ago and now wokeness dwindled in brands and entertainment
items.summary: The post notes corporations like Bud Light, Netflix, and others abandoning DEI initiatives, race-based hiring, and woke policies after public backlash. It attributes this to the silent majority becoming vocal, diminishing wokeness across entertainment and business. Paramount's avoidance of altering classics is cited as progress.

items.title: Entertainment industry’s woke mind virus causing collapse with Disney Snow White flop
items.summary: The thread describes Hollywood's shift to prioritizing social credit over profit, infected by the woke mind virus, leading to propaganda disguised as entertainment. Disney's Snow White remake lost $170M amid backlash, contributing to 2025 box office failure. It predicts industry necrosis unless refocused on entertainment.

items.title: Paperclip: Open-Source OS for Running Zero-Employee AI Companies
items.summary: Paperclip is an open-sourced operating system that enables users to launch fully autonomous companies staffed by AI agents in roles like CEO, CTO, engineers, and marketers, complete with org charts, budgets, governance, and accountability features. It addresses key pain points such as context loss, runaway costs, and agent orchestration through heartbeats, ticket systems, and goal alignment. An upcoming Clipmart marketplace will allow one-click deployment of pre-built company templates, making it a game-changer for solopreneurs and small business builders.

items.title: Small Business Owners Quietly Building Custom AI Tools for Massive Savings
items.summary: Non-technical small business owners are creating bespoke AI solutions like receptionists saving $4k/month for dentists, demand predictors cutting food truck waste by 40%, style-matching editors doubling photographer bookings, churn predictors boosting gym retention by 22%, and custom CRMs replacing expensive software. These real-world examples demonstrate tangible impacts without professional coding skills. The divide between builders and observers is widening into a survival gap.

items.title: Every Launches AI-Native Back Office Agents for Startups and Small Businesses
items.summary: Every unveiled AI CFO, AI Bookkeeper, and AI CHRO agents to handle banking, payroll, HR compliance, accounting, and taxes for startups and small businesses, eliminating the need for extra staff. These agents deliver real-time financial insights, automated bookkeeping, and compliance checks via an integrated platform for superior context-aware performance. By consolidating fragmented tools and slashing overhead, it frees owners to prioritize growth.

items.title: Intuit Launches AI-Powered ERP Solution Tailored for Construction Small Businesses
items.summary: Intuit introduced Construction Edition of its Enterprise Suite, an AI-native ERP unifying project management, finances, and operations for mid-market construction firms outgrowing QuickBooks. Features include AI-driven cost proposals, invoicing, budgeting, and industry-specific workflows to streamline scaling. This meaningful product move enhances efficiency for small construction businesses handling complex operations.
